Diagram of a Pearson Square. A large square box. In the exact centre is the number "16% (Target)". At the top left corner outside the box is "Sorghum (10%)". At the bottom left is "Fish meal (70%)". Diagonal arrows cross the box: from 70 up to the top right, and from 10 down to the bottom right. At the top right corner is the calculation "70 - 16 = 54 parts of Sorghum". At the bottom right corner is "16 - 10 = 6 parts of Fish meal". Below the square is written: "Total parts = 54 + 6 = 60".

Split illustration showing forage conservation methods. On the left (Hay making): a sunny field where a farmer is turning dry, yellowish cut grass with a pitchfork, and rectangular bales are stacked in a wooden shed. On the right (Silage making): a trench dug into the ground filled with chopped green maize plants; a tractor is driving over it to compact it, and one section is covered with a black plastic sheet weighted down with soil.
